A skill is a workflow: the house way to do one whole job (triage an alarm, troubleshoot a component)
with the [MCP tools](/reference/mcp/). The server serves each one as an MCP prompt, so an agent's
client lists them beside the tools, and `omniglass mcp skill <name>` prints one for an agent
that reads skill files instead. A skill runs nothing itself: it tells the agent which tools to call,
and each call is gated, scoped and audited as any other. The tools and permissions below are read
from the tool catalog, so a skill can never claim less than its tools need. To use one, see
[connect an agent](/guides/agents/#skills).

2 skills.

| Skill | Category | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| [`triage-alarm`](#triage-alarm) | operate | Work out whether a component's alarm is real, what caused it, and what the operator should do next, reading before any change. |
| [`troubleshoot-component`](#troubleshoot-component) | operate | Diagnose a component that is misbehaving, from whether omniglass can reach it to what its own measurements say, and propose a fix. |

## `triage-alarm`

Work out whether a component's alarm is real, what caused it, and what the operator should do next, reading before any change.

- Category: operate
- Arguments:
  - `component` (required): The component carrying the alarm, by name
  - `alarm` (optional): The alarm to triage, by its rule or message, when the component has more than one
- Tools: [`get-component`](/reference/mcp/#get-component) (`component:read`), [`list-component-alarms`](/reference/mcp/#list-component-alarms) (`component:read`), [`get-component-reachability`](/reference/mcp/#get-component-reachability) (`component:read`), [`list-endpoints`](/reference/mcp/#list-endpoints) (`endpoint:read`), [`get-endpoint`](/reference/mcp/#get-endpoint) (`endpoint:read`), [`get-node`](/reference/mcp/#get-node) (`node:read`), [`list-component-events`](/reference/mcp/#list-component-events) (`component:read`), [`list-component-logs`](/reference/mcp/#list-component-logs) (`component:read`), [`list-component-metric-series`](/reference/mcp/#list-component-metric-series) (`component:read`), [`list-component-property-series`](/reference/mcp/#list-component-property-series) (`component:read`), [`list-component-dependencies`](/reference/mcp/#list-component-dependencies) (`component:read`), [`run-endpoint-poll`](/reference/mcp/#run-endpoint-poll) (`endpoint:run`), [`list-component-commands`](/reference/mcp/#list-component-commands) (`command:read`), [`issue-component-command`](/reference/mcp/#issue-component-command) (`command:issue`)
- Permissions: `component:read`, `endpoint:read`, `node:read`, `endpoint:run`, `command:read`, `command:issue`

### Triage an alarm

An alarm is the component's own verdict that something is wrong. Triage answers
three questions in order: is it still true, what caused it, and what should
happen now. Read everything first; change nothing until the operator agrees.

#### 1. Confirm the alarm

Read the component with [`get-component`](/reference/mcp/#get-component), then its active alarms with
[`list-component-alarms`](/reference/mcp/#list-component-alarms). If the alarm named is not in the active set, read
again with `include_cleared` set: it may have cleared on its own, and a
flapping alarm (raised and cleared over and over) is a finding in itself.
Say which alarm you are triaging, when it was raised, and its severity.

#### 2. Is the component reachable?

Read [`get-component-reachability`](/reference/mcp/#get-component-reachability). An unreachable component explains
most alarms on it at once: the cause is the path to it (the node, the network,
the endpoint), not the thing the alarm names. If it is unreachable, read the
endpoint it is polled through with [`list-endpoints`](/reference/mcp/#list-endpoints) and [`get-endpoint`](/reference/mcp/#get-endpoint),
and the node that polls it with [`get-node`](/reference/mcp/#get-node).

#### 3. Find what changed

Read what led up to the alarm, in the window before it was raised:

- the events, with [`list-component-events`](/reference/mcp/#list-component-events);
- the logs, with [`list-component-logs`](/reference/mcp/#list-component-logs), filtered to warnings and above first;
- the measurement the alarm is about, with [`list-component-metric-series`](/reference/mcp/#list-component-metric-series)
  or [`list-component-property-series`](/reference/mcp/#list-component-property-series), to see whether it crossed a line or
  stopped reporting.

#### 4. Check the blast radius

Read what depends on the component with [`list-component-dependencies`](/reference/mcp/#list-component-dependencies). An
alarm on a component other things depend on is the root; alarms on its
dependents are symptoms. Say which you are looking at.

#### 5. Recommend, then wait

Report: the alarm, whether it is still true, the most likely cause with the
evidence for it, and what is affected. Then propose one next step:

- a fresh poll, to confirm a fix took, with [`run-endpoint-poll`](/reference/mcp/#run-endpoint-poll);
- a command the component's driver offers, from [`list-component-commands`](/reference/mcp/#list-component-commands);
- acknowledging or snoozing the alarm in the console, when the cause is known
  and someone owns it;
- or handing it to a person, saying what they need to look at.

Ask before any of these. A poll and a command change what the component does;
issue a command with [`issue-component-command`](/reference/mcp/#issue-component-command) only after the operator
says yes to that exact command. Never ask for, read, or repeat a credential:
the poll and the command run on the server with the credentials bound to the
endpoint, and you only need to know they are there.

## `troubleshoot-component`

Diagnose a component that is misbehaving, from whether omniglass can reach it to what its own measurements say, and propose a fix.

- Category: operate
- Arguments:
  - `component` (required): The component to troubleshoot, by name
  - `symptom` (optional): What the operator saw, in their words
- Tools: [`get-component`](/reference/mcp/#get-component) (`component:read`), [`get-system-health`](/reference/mcp/#get-system-health) (`system:read`), [`get-component-reachability`](/reference/mcp/#get-component-reachability) (`component:read`), [`list-endpoints`](/reference/mcp/#list-endpoints) (`endpoint:read`), [`get-endpoint`](/reference/mcp/#get-endpoint) (`endpoint:read`), [`get-node`](/reference/mcp/#get-node) (`node:read`), [`list-node-logs`](/reference/mcp/#list-node-logs) (`node:read`), [`list-component-properties`](/reference/mcp/#list-component-properties) (`component:read`), [`list-component-metrics`](/reference/mcp/#list-component-metrics) (`component:read`), [`list-component-property-series`](/reference/mcp/#list-component-property-series) (`component:read`), [`list-component-metric-series`](/reference/mcp/#list-component-metric-series) (`component:read`), [`list-component-alarms`](/reference/mcp/#list-component-alarms) (`component:read`), [`list-component-events`](/reference/mcp/#list-component-events) (`component:read`), [`list-component-logs`](/reference/mcp/#list-component-logs) (`component:read`), [`list-component-dependencies`](/reference/mcp/#list-component-dependencies) (`component:read`), [`run-endpoint-poll`](/reference/mcp/#run-endpoint-poll) (`endpoint:run`), [`list-component-commands`](/reference/mcp/#list-component-commands) (`command:read`), [`issue-component-command`](/reference/mcp/#issue-component-command) (`command:issue`)
- Permissions: `component:read`, `system:read`, `endpoint:read`, `node:read`, `endpoint:run`, `command:read`, `command:issue`

### Troubleshoot a component

Work from the outside in: first whether omniglass can see the component at all,
then what it says about itself, then what is around it. Each step rules out a
layer, so stop and report as soon as one explains the symptom.

#### 1. Know what you are looking at

Read the component with [`get-component`](/reference/mcp/#get-component): its type, its product, where it
is, and the system it belongs to. If it belongs to a system, read the system's
health with [`get-system-health`](/reference/mcp/#get-system-health); if the whole system is unhealthy, the
component may be one symptom of a wider fault.

#### 2. Can omniglass reach it?

Read [`get-component-reachability`](/reference/mcp/#get-component-reachability). If it is unreachable:

- read the endpoints with [`list-endpoints`](/reference/mcp/#list-endpoints) and the one this component uses
  with [`get-endpoint`](/reference/mcp/#get-endpoint): its last poll result says whether the poll failed
  to connect, was refused, or got an answer it could not read;
- read the node that polls it with [`get-node`](/reference/mcp/#get-node), and that node's logs with
  [`list-node-logs`](/reference/mcp/#list-node-logs): a node that is down or cannot route to the component
  makes every component behind it unreachable.

#### 3. What does it say about itself?

Read the current state with [`list-component-properties`](/reference/mcp/#list-component-properties) and
[`list-component-metrics`](/reference/mcp/#list-component-metrics), and how it got there with
[`list-component-property-series`](/reference/mcp/#list-component-property-series) and [`list-component-metric-series`](/reference/mcp/#list-component-metric-series).
Read its alarms with [`list-component-alarms`](/reference/mcp/#list-component-alarms), its events with
[`list-component-events`](/reference/mcp/#list-component-events), and its logs with [`list-component-logs`](/reference/mcp/#list-component-logs).
Line the symptom up against these: the first measurement or event that changed
before the symptom started is the lead.

#### 4. What is around it?

Read its dependencies with [`list-component-dependencies`](/reference/mcp/#list-component-dependencies). A component
that depends on a faulted one inherits its fault; fix the one it depends on.

#### 5. Propose a fix, then wait

Say what you found, layer by layer, and which layer the fault is in. Propose
the smallest next step: a fresh poll with [`run-endpoint-poll`](/reference/mcp/#run-endpoint-poll) to check
the fault is still there, or a command from [`list-component-commands`](/reference/mcp/#list-component-commands)
(a reboot, an input change) issued with [`issue-component-command`](/reference/mcp/#issue-component-command). Ask
before each one, naming exactly what it will do. Never ask for, read, or
repeat a credential: the server polls and commands with the credentials bound
to the endpoint, and you only need to know they are there.
